messages:
arya: Heads-up — noticed a reconnect spike in EU after the backpressure patch rolled. Dashboard shows a sudden burst of short lived connections that then reconnect -> duplicate billing counts. https://internal.redwood/d/streaming/reconnects (low level).

josh: Seen it too. Logs show route tag flips mid-session from \"fingerprint_v2\" -> \"fallback\" which triggers a resume flow and a new lease. snippet: \n```\n2026-03-20T15:02:12Z session=abc123 route=fingerprint_v2 event=idle
2026-03-20T15:02:13Z session=abc123 route=fallback event=reconnect reason=route_changed
```

maggie: Is the billing double-counting coming from resume creating a new token or from prefix cache eviction?

pierce: Looks like route priority heuristics are using a per-request fingerprint that can change when the client probes or a header changes. When that flip happens the proxy treats it as a different backend and we run the resume-negotiation which duplicates tokens.

sre-bot: alert: streaming.reconnects.rate > 3x baseline in eu-west-1 for last 10m (threshold 50/min).

arya: Repro (dev): run: `curl -N -H \"X-Fingerprint: fpA\" https://stream.redwood/test/sse` then in a second request change header to `fpB` using same client session id. server logs: route flip -> resume.

josh: Minimal config that surfaces it:
```yaml
streaming: 
  route_priority: [fingerprint, capacity]
  allow_route_change_resume: true
```

maggie: console shows reconnections tagged under two different route versions so the dashboard aggregation loses the \"single session\" identity. We need a resume_id or session_guid propagated to metrics so counts can be deduped.

pierce: Agreed. Two parts: 1) short-term mitigation: prefer sticky routing on session-id to avoid mid-session fingerprint changes. 2) longer: update telemetry to include `session_guid`, `route_version`, and `resume_id` so console can de-dup.

arya: Proposed quick patch (canary): add sticky_session preference with TTL=5m and set it for 5% of traffic in eu-west-1. Config flag: `feature.streaming.sticky_routes_v1` (FF).

josh: Also thinking about caller UX: if resume is necessary we should emit a metric `stream.resume.duplicate_charge` and surface it in the console rollup + alert. That will help ops triage during canary.

maggie: For dashboards: add panel that counts unique `session_guid` per minute vs reconnect events per minute. If reconnects >> unique sessions then we know duplication is occurring.

pierce: Canary plan:
- enable FF at 5% in eu-west-1 for 48h
- add `session_guid` tag to all resume/route-change spans (temporary retention 7d)
- create console panel and alert for `reconnects / unique_sessions > 1.2`
- monitor billing_diff: `billing.tokens.duplicated.rate`

arya: Rollback plan: kill FF, revert allow_route_change_resume=true (set false) if canary spikes reconnects. Also we need a hotfix: when route flips mid-session, don't treat it as new chargeable resume if `session_guid` matches — just migrate without issuing a new token.

sre-bot: note: please @eng-runtime and @billing on the canary start.

console-bot: created dashboard card \"streaming: session dedupe\" and added to eng-platform home. link: https://internal.redwood/dash/streaming-dedupe

josh: Anyone object to shipping sticky_session for short-term? small config change, low risk.

maggie: No objections. +1 for telemetry tags too. Need to coordinate with billing to ensure we don't double-bill while we iterate.

pierce: I'll open PR for sticky routing + session_guid tagging and include migration test. Target deploy window tuesday midnight UTC to minimize customer impact.

arya: Thanks — I'll prepare the FF rollout doc and add the console panels. We'll review results after 24h and either expand or rollback. :thumbsup:
